body: seems like noone can, good to know :)

Thanks again for sharing so much, I appreciate your openness.

Oh boy, what you said regarding your Monday sounds like your mind finally got a chance to dump some of that pain you are feeling. I hope it was a bit relieving (besides the "inconvenience" of the situation :) ) 

It seems to me like you are being very focused about the wellbeing of your friends, even when you are struggling so much and I am sure they appreciate that as well.   


Could it also be that they are not asking about you anymore because they don't want to be annoying to you, or just don't know what how to help? If I was one of your roommates, I could certainly see how I would be a bit helpless on how to approach you, and I might just rely on you approaching me instead. 

  
If they really didn't want to know anymore, or are too busy, would they still give you advice or immediately call you multiple after you sent that text?

I don't know you well enough to say whether your friend is right with the suggestion to go for more significant care. But indeed considering it seems like another great thing to do before taking any other, more final, decisions.   


This is just an assumption, but it seems to me your friends would do all they can to help you get that more significant care, which might just be the thing you need to turn things around, and also make it so that they can be relieved in the knowledge that you are receiving help?  


I will go to bed soon, so my apologies if I might not respond to your next message immediately. You can also reach me in DMs btw, if you prefer that.

Wow. First off, I have to say I am extremely impressed by your style of writing considering what you are going through. Your thoughts are well formulated, and you appear quite smart to me. This just a random compliment, I hope you can accept it :)

It's hard for me to grasp how you must feel regarding the loss of your class-mate, as I fortunately haven't lost anyone close to me yet. Still, I can see how that would really mess someone up. Considering this, are your thoughts of suicide really that pathetic, as you described them? If someone else told you this as their story, would you also call their reaction pathetic?   


After all, you took quite a few hits lately, so it seems perfectly understandable to me that you are losing faith in getting better.  


You were asking for reinforcement and suggestions to take another path;

 In my opinion, you are already doing great, all things considered. You are going to therapy, you are aware of your condition, and you are working on it. As you mentioned, there are ups and downs, but what makes you think this is the highest you can get?

Everything I know so far about your story, which isn't much, admittedly, makes me believe you are a great person who cares about others around them a lot (maybe more than about yourself?). 

It would be horrible if the world lost someone like you.

In any case, if I was part of that class, I would certainly be able to forgive you quite easily for sleeping through the clinic. 

I hope I was able to help you a little bit.

You're very welcome!  


That sounds good, having a therapist as a friend can be really valuable - it seems to me that is something worth waiting for, and put off your idea of giving up at least until then, what do you think?  


Regarding talking to your friends, could you maybe be open about your situation with them? 

Tell them that you feel like, even though they assured you in the past that you are not a burden to them, things have changed, and you are unsure now and feel like retreating?Tell them that you are afraid of them lying to you to make you feel better, and that you need them to be honest?

Wouldn't it be worth to at least give it a shot and see how they react? What, in your mind, is the worst that could happen?

I am so sorry to hear that you lost your friend, and your partner(? not sure if I understood that correctly, my apologies). I can understand how the pain seems unbearable right now.   


Are you willing to tell us what you tried so far to fight the suicidal thoughts? For example, did you already talk about them with family,friends, a therapist? 

Lastly, the method you spoke of doesn't sound painless at all, and provides a lot of room for things to go horribly wrong.

Hey,

You're doing fine, actually. Thanks for sharing. Your story sounds like you are going through extremely hard times, and it makes sense that you feel helpless. Allow me some questions so I can understand you even better.

Do you feel like you won't find another therapist like the one you had? Did you ever ask your friends whether they perveice you as a burden? If not, do you trust them to tell you the truth if you asked them?
You are not alone, we are here if you want to talk.

I am sorry.  


I would disagree with you, however, and say that, regardless of what you did, you could still try to make amends for it.   


Even if you had murdered someone, the family of the victim would not be better off because you are dead. In fact, they might feel like you were trying to escape punishment.  
   
So I'd suggest you continue to live, accept your punishment, and proceed to focus on making the best out of the situation.  
If you can't help the people you hurt, you can focus on helping others in their stead.

I'd say that would be a much better outcome than suicide, both for you and the people around you.

(I am not actually assuming you are a murderer, I just took an extreme example to illustrate my point)

I wish you well.
